items.subtype: adjective complement with the fixed preposition responsible for
items.sentence: The agency is responsible of monitoring water quality near the reservoir.
items.answer_explanation: The adjective responsible takes the fixed preposition for before its gerund complement.

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement with a plural subject
items.sentence: The buses that travels along the old route carry commuters into the city each morning.
items.answer_explanation: The relative-clause subject that refers to the plural noun buses, so the finite verb must be travel.

items.subtype: parallel finite verbs in a coordinated predicate
items.sentence: The committee reviewed the proposal and approving the revised budget after the public hearing.

marked_parts.D: the revised budget after the public hearing

items.answer_explanation: The coordinated predicates share the past-tense subject committee, so reviewed and approved must be parallel finite verbs.

items.subtype: plural noun after a plural quantifier
items.sentence: The archivist cataloged several traditional tale from the mountain region.
items.answer_explanation: The quantifier several requires a countable plural noun, so tale must be changed to tales.

items.subtype: past participle after a modal perfect construction
items.sentence: By the time the survey ended, the geologists concluded that the glacier had melt substantially.

marked_parts.A: By the time the survey ended

items.answer_explanation: The auxiliary had must be followed by the past participle melted, not the bare form melt.

items.subtype: adjective order inside a noun phrase
items.sentence: The treatment plant replaced a concrete ancient pipe beneath the filtration basin.
items.answer_explanation: In this noun phrase, the age adjective ancient precedes the material adjective concrete, and the article changes to an.
